title: What does selection add?
hook: Keep anyone with X or Y. What happens to the relationship inside that group?

knows: arithmetic means, rates and simple plotted values
doesNotKnow: show how filtering a dataset adds a hidden collider to the graph.

misconception: Treating add a selection node as valid without checking the stated model, denominators or causal assumptions.
objective: show how filtering a dataset adds a hidden collider to the graph.
keyState: Both finite cases completed; their computed summaries retained.

claims.text: Independent fair binary X,Y produce four equally likely worlds. Keep a world if X or Y is 1. Among selected worlds with X=0, what is P(Y=1)?
claims.source: src/demos/probability/p100-add-a-selection-node/spec.ts; exact finite illustration specified in manager numericCase: IndependentX,Y binary; selectionS=1 iffXorY. Full4 worlds give independent; selected3 worlds yieldP(Y1|X1)=.5 vsP(Y1|X0)=1. Show selection-node collider and retained rows.

claims.text: Selection retains P(Y=1|X=0)=100%; the full population retains 50%. In the selected set, a zero X can enter only alongside a one Y.
claims.source: src/demos/probability/p100-add-a-selection-node/spec.ts; exact finite illustration specified in manager numericCase: IndependentX,Y binary; selectionS=1 iffXorY. Full4 worlds give independent; selected3 worlds yieldP(Y1|X1)=.5 vsP(Y1|X0)=1. Show selection-node collider and retained rows.

claims.text: The selection rule is a shared effect of X and Y. Conditioning on entry opens that collider and creates dependence between originally independent variables. Adding a selection node makes the filtering operation part of the causal story.
claims.source: src/demos/probability/p100-add-a-selection-node/spec.ts; exact finite illustration specified in manager numericCase: IndependentX,Y binary; selectionS=1 iffXorY. Full4 worlds give independent; selected3 worlds yieldP(Y1|X1)=.5 vsP(Y1|X0)=1. Show selection-node collider and retained rows.

claims.text: A sample includes anyone strong OR fast. Among sampled people who are not strong, what must be true? The OR admission rule requires speed when strength is absent.
